info.name: Hot Metal — Provisioner
info.description:
# Hot Metal Provisioner Service

The Provisioner (`hotmetal-provisioner`) owns the per-publication EmDash fleet on Cloudflare Workers for Platforms: it holds the scoped `CF_API_TOKEN`, runs the `ProvisionWorkflow` (create D1/R2/KV → upload tenant script → first-boot migrate → headless bootstrap → store credentials → mark ready), and tears tenants down. One publication == one dedicated EmDash tenant (`pub-<id>` script + `emdash-tenant/media/session-<id>` infra) served at `<slug>.hotmetalapp.com`.

## Authentication

All `/api/*` endpoints require `Authorization: Bearer <token>` matching the `API_KEY` secret on the provisioner worker (the same value web carries as `PROVISIONER_API_KEY`). `/health` is unauthenticated.

The provisioner is normally reached service-binding-only (web → provisioner); set `PROVISIONER_BASE_URL` to whatever URL you expose it on for direct admin calls.

## Endpoints Overview

| Method | Path | Auth | Description |
|--------|------|------|-------------|
| GET | `/health` | None | Service health check |
| POST | `/api/provision` | Bearer | Start (or report in-flight) provisioning for a publication |
| GET | `/api/provision/:publicationId/status` | Bearer | Provisioning state for the dashboard |
| POST | `/api/teardown` | Bearer | Tear down a tenant's infra (deprovision) |
| POST | `/api/fleet/upgrade` | Bearer | Roll the shared bundle out to a list / all ready tenants |

## Environment Variables

- `PROVISIONER_BASE_URL` — Base URL of the provisioner worker.
- `PROVISIONER_API_KEY` — Bearer token (must match the provisioner `API_KEY` secret).
- `publicationId` — collection variable for chaining requests.

item.name: Provisioning
item.description: Create, inspect, and tear down a publication's dedicated EmDash tenant. All endpoints inherit Bearer authentication from the collection.

item.name: Provision — Start / Retry
item.description:
Kick off provisioning for a publication. Idempotent-ish:
- If the publication is already `ready`, no-ops (`alreadyProvisioned:true`).
- A `create` trigger uses a deterministic workflow id (`pub-<id>`) so duplicate create events dedupe; if one is already running it reports `inFlight:true`.
- `manual`/`retry` get a fresh workflow id so an operator can re-run a failed/stuck provision. A retry also re-uploads the tenant script (handy after a binding/bundle change).

### Request Body

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------------|
| `publicationId` | string | **Yes** | Publication to provision. Must exist. |
| `triggeredBy` | string | No | `create` \| `manual` \| `retry` (default `manual`). |

### Errors
- `400` — missing `publicationId`
- `401` — bad bearer token
- `404` — publication not found

item.name: Teardown — Deprovision
item.description:
Tear down a tenant's infra (dispatch script + R2 + D1 + KV). Used for admin / failed-provision cleanup and as the deprovision-on-delete path (web calls this with `force:true` BEFORE deleting the publication, while the instance meta is still available).

`force:true` is required to tear down a `ready` or `provisioning` instance. Already-gone (404) resources count as success; real failures are reported in `failed[]` and the instance meta is kept so the teardown stays retryable.

### Request Body
| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------------|
| `publicationId` | string | **Yes** | EmDash publication to tear down |
| `force` | boolean | No | Required (`true`) for a `ready`/`provisioning` instance |

### Errors
- `400` — missing `publicationId`, or publication is not an EmDash instance
- `401` — bad bearer token
- `404` — publication not found
- `409` — refusing to tear down a `ready`/`provisioning` instance without `force:true`
- `500` — partial teardown (see `failed[]`)

response.name: 409 — Force required

item.name: Fleet
item.description: Fleet-wide bundle rollout. Inherits Bearer authentication from the collection.

item.name: Fleet Upgrade — Rollout bundle
item.description:
Re-deploy the current shared EmDash bundle to a LIST of tenants (canary) or ALL ready tenants. A pure script re-upload — it reconstructs each tenant's bindings from `cms_instance_meta`, re-uploads the bundle, and bumps `cms_instance_meta.bundleVersion`. It does **not** run bootstrap (no PAT rotation) and never touches tenant D1/data.

Per-tenant failures are reported, never abort the batch. **Release the new bundle first** (`pnpm release-bundle`), then canary a subset, then roll to all.

### Request Body
| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------------|
| `publicationIds` | string[] | One of | Explicit tenants to upgrade (canary). Mutually exclusive with `all`. |
| `all` | boolean | One of | Upgrade every `emdash`+`ready` tenant. Mutually exclusive with `publicationIds`. |
| `version` | string | No | Bundle release to deploy. Defaults to `EMDASH_BUNDLE_VERSION`. Allowed chars: letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-`. |

Exactly one of `publicationIds` (non-empty) / `all:true` must be provided.

### Response
`{ version, targeted, upgraded[], failed[], skipped[] }` where `targeted == upgraded.length + failed.length`.
- **skipped** — requested id not found / not `emdash` / not `ready`.
- **failed** — `ready` tenant with missing/malformed `cms_instance_meta`, or whose upload threw.

### Status codes
- `200` — all targeted tenants upgraded, or nothing to do
- `207` — partial: some tenants failed (inspect `failed[]`)
- `502` — every targeted tenant failed
- `400` — bad target selection (both/neither of `all`/`publicationIds`), invalid JSON, unknown/invalid `version`
- `401` — bad bearer token

response.name: 207 — Partial
